changelog: Replace C7 to explicitly demote cuts that separate scope-bearing operators (negation, modals, auxiliaries, quantifiers, complementizers) from their arguments or complements when the pre-cut span would assert a claim — addresses the primary finding about stranded predicates/obligatory complements causing contradictions.
findings: The prompt treats head–complement splits too crudely: it does not consistently recognize when a predicate, required complement, or scope-bearing operator (objects, prepositional complements, negation, complement clauses) is cohesion-critical, so cuts that strand these elements are ranked as if harmless and produce misleading or contradictory fragments.

edits.was: - Negation and narrow-focus devices in English often await auxiliaries or follow
edits.now: - Demote cuts that separate scope-bearing operators (negation, modals, auxiliari

diagnosis.why: Replacing C7 to demote cuts that separate scope-bearing operators made the model avoid cutting immediately after verbs/modals/negation and instead shift cuts rightward into their complements or inside noun/prepositional phrases; that reduced contradictions in some long/clause-level cases but produced more bad tiny fragments overall, with the harm concentrated in short–medium latency bins (≤5 and ≤7) as shown by the by_bin and the larger n_worse than n_better.
diagnosis.lesson: A later revision should keep scope-bearing operators attached when necessary but not indiscriminately push cuts into short/medium-length complements or inside noun/prepositional phrases (the ≤5–≤7 bins), since that rightward shift creates many small, low-cohesion fragments.
